items.title: 61539_Butter Jackson oral history interview
items.q: He left the band in '44 to go to Harry James.

ctx.x: Well, Johnny Hodges left to get his own band. We was playing the Thunderbird out in Vegas at the

time and I noticed that Juan Tizol, I see him come back stage and talk to Duke, you know, because he had been with Duke from 1929 up until about '44. He left the band in '44 to go to Harry James. So I knew they was very good friends because he used to do all the Duke's copying and everything and, you know, Tizol wrote a lot of tunes in that book, too, you know. Tizol had quite a few tunes in there. He was the co-writer of 'Caravan'. He wrote Pyramid. He wrote 'Conga Brava'. He wrote 'Fiesta in Blue' and…

So I saw him come back stage and I said, 'Now, something is funny here because Johnny's leaving,' and Sonny Greer was gone with Johnny and Lawrence left to go with Johnny. So they didn't send all the way back to New York for a trombone player, they sent to Los Angeles because it was close to Frisco and got Britt Woodman. And at that time Claude Jones had came back.
